post.caption:
Every human hand has an involuntary tremor that never stops, and at the scale of stitching a blood vessel it is enormous. A surgical robot reads the surgeon's movement, filters the tremor out and scales the rest down, so a centimetre of hand becomes a millimetre of instrument. The surgeon is still driving all of it. Industrial arms do the other version: the same movement to fractions of a millimetre, for years, with no fatigue or drift. Amplifiers, not replacements.
